707713.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kléwos (whence Mycenaean Greek 𐀐𐀩𐀺 (ke-re-wo)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱléwos.

707714.t: From κλεπ- (klep-, present stem of κλέπτω (kléptō, “to steal”)) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix).

707715.t: From Proto-Hellenic *klépt͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *klép-ye-ti, from *klep-. Cognates include Latin clepō and Gothic 𐌷𐌻𐌹𐍆𐌰𐌽 (hlifan).

707784.t: Uncertain; possibly from Pre-Greek. Potential cognates include Spanish cuesco (“stone (of fruit)”), though this is rejected by Furnee.

707772.t: From Proto-Hellenic *koňňós, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱomyós, from *ḱóm (“with”) + *-yós (“adjectival suffix”), the ancestor of the suffix -ιος (-ios). Cognates include Latin cum, Gaulish com-, and Old English ge-.

707709.t: From Proto-Hellenic *klāwī́ds, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u- (“nail; pin; hook”, instruments, of old use for locking doors). Cognate with Latin clāvus (“nail; pin”), Old Church Slavonic ключь (ključĭ, “key”).

707781.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱey- (“to lie down”), the same root of κεῖμαι (keîmai, “to lie in a place”).

707744.t: From Proto-Indo-European *klūd-. Cognates include Gothic 𐌷𐌻𐌿𐍄𐍂𐍃 (hlūtrs), Welsh clir, and Latin cluō, clovāca.

707727.t: Of disputed origin: * Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂-, a metathesized form of *kelh₂- (“to hit, cut down”).

707707.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₂- (“to beat, break”), whence also Latin percellō (“to beat down, overturn”), but due to phonetic difficulties, Beekes prefers to take the verb as Pre-Greek.

707702.t: Apparently from a Proto-Hellenic *klə́dos, from Proto-Indo-European *kl̥d-o-s (“piece of wood”), which is traditionally linked to *kelh₂- (“to break”).

707704.t: From κλάω (klắō, “to break”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

707767.t: Perhaps from an unattested *κοῖμος (*koîmos) or *κοιμή (*koimḗ) -άω (-ắō). The base of the verb may have derived from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱey- (“to lie down”).

707753.t: Traditionally derived from κνίζω (knízō, “scratch or gash”); yet the -ι- is long in this word, which may point to Pre-Greek origin, according to Beekes.

707701.t: Attested in Mycenaean Greek 𐀑𐀺 (ki-wo). From Proto-Indo-European *ḱiHwon-, whence also Old Armenian սիւն (siwn, “column; pillar”).

707762.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱowilos, from *ḱewH- (“hollow”) (which may be identical to *ḱewh₁- (“to swell”)).

707703.t: Stems: * κλαϝ- > κλα- (κλάω (klā́ō)) / κλαυ- (κλαυ-θμός (klau-thmós)) * κλαϝ-j- > κλαι- * κλαϝ-σ- > κλαυσ- (the future κλαύσω (klaúsō), κλαυσι-) * κλαϝ-ε- > κλαϝ-ε-σ- > the future κλαήσω (klaḗsō). Uncertain etymology.

707750.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kónh₂m (“leg”); cognate with English ham (from Proto-Germanic *hammō) and Old Irish cnáim (“bone”).

707710.t: From Proto-Hellenic *klāyyō, from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂uyeti, from *kleh₂u- (“hook, key”), whence κληΐς (klēḯs), κλήϊθρον (klḗïthron).

707746.t: Uncertain. Has been connected with Ancient Greek κάλαθος (kálathos) and Latin colus, although Beekes rejects these connections.

707711.t: From κλέπτω (kléptō, “to steal”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

707739.t: From the root of κλίνω (klī́nō, “to lie down; to recline”).

707720.t: Traditionally connected with κλάω (kláō, “to break”), but the semantics are tenuous, and there is no evidence for a long α (a) in the former. Thus, Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

707741.t: Often connected to κλείς (kleís, “key”). Alternatively, the word could be Pre-Greek.

707756.t: Frisk assumed that this word and κνώδων (knṓdōn, “projecting teeth on the blade of a hunting spear”), κνώδαξ (knṓdax, “pin, pivot”) go back to a verbal noun *κνωδ- (*knōd-, “tooth, biter, gnawer”), belonging to κναίω (knaíō, “to scrape, scratch”).

707755.t: Based on the stem forms κνιδ-, κνισ- (knid-, knis-), likely from a Proto-Indo-European *kneyd- (“to scratch, knock”), from *ken- (“to scratch; scrape; rub”).

707777.t: Back-formation from κοινωνέω (koinōnéō), after pairs like στρατηγέω (stratēgéō) and στρατηγός (stratēgós).
